speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; please tell me, how long have you been experiencing this swelling, and does it worsen after physical activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very young age for simple swelling. Given the family history of similar issues and the onset after minor activity, could you describe if the knee is red, warm to the touch, or if the child has a limp? Also, has he experienced any fever or other joint pain recently?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_X-Ray_Right.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inflammatory markers and X-ray results are normal, which effectively rules out infection like tuberculosis and acute trauma. Given the patient's age of 18 months, the sudden onset of swelling without injury, and the strong family history, could you describe the range of motion in the knee or if the joint feels "stiff" compared to the other leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal inflammatory markers and X-ray, combined with the painless swelling in a toddler with a family history, strongly suggest a specific bone disorder. Does the child have a limp or refuse to bear weight on the right leg? Additionally, is the swelling located specifically at the head of the femur?

REQUEST TEST: MRI of the right knee to assess for bone marrow edema and subchondral insufficiency fracture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the right knee: Findings consistent with spontaneous subchondral insufficiency fracture of the capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE-like presentation), characterized by bone marrow edema and a linear hypointense fracture line at the superior aspect of the right femoral head. No joint effusion or acute septic changes observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Spontaneous Subchondral Insufficiency Fracture of the Femoral Head.
